note: Every entry carries the instrument it comes from and the date it was last checked. 'confidence: primary' means the instrument itself was read. 'confidence: reported' means a secondary source was read and the instrument was not. Nothing is listed without a source.

deadlines.title: Article 14 reporting duty goes live
deadlines.summary: Manufacturers must report actively exploited vulnerabilities within 24 hours and severe incidents within 24 hours, through the ENISA single reporting platform.
deadlines.penalty: Article 64 fine tier applies from 11 December 2027: up to €15m or 2.5% of worldwide turnover. Until then the exposure is market surveillance action under Articles 54 and 58.

deadlines.title: Article 64 penalties become applicable
deadlines.summary: The full Regulation applies from this date. Article 64 fines attach to non-compliance with Article 14, up to €15m or 2.5% of worldwide annual turnover, whichever is higher.
deadlines.penalty: €15m or 2.5% (Annex I, Articles 13 and 14); €10m or 2%; €5m or 1%.

deadlines.title: High-risk AI obligations — Annex III standalone systems
deadlines.summary: Conformity assessment, technical documentation and EU database registration for standalone high-risk systems: hiring, credit scoring, education, essential services, biometrics, law enforcement. Deferred from 2 August 2026 by the Digital Omnibus on AI.
deadlines.penalty: Up to €15m or 3% of worldwide turnover for prohibited practices; €35m or 7% for the prohibitions in Article 5. High-risk breaches sit at €15m or 3%.

source.label: Regulation (EU) 2026/1744 amending Regulation (EU) 2024/1689; in force 27 July 2026

deadlines.title: High-risk AI obligations — Annex I product-embedded systems
deadlines.summary: High-risk obligations for AI embedded in products already covered by EU product-safety law: medical devices, machinery, toys, lifts. Deferred from 2 August 2027.
deadlines.penalty: €15m or 3% of worldwide turnover.

deadlines.title: Article 50(2) transition period ends — AI content marking
deadlines.summary: Systems placed on the market before 2 August 2026 must comply with the Article 50(2) obligation to mark synthetic audio, image, video and text in a machine-readable format.
deadlines.penalty: €15m or 3% of worldwide turnover.

deadlines.title: New product liability regime applies — software becomes a product
deadlines.summary: Directive (EU) 2024/2853 applies. Software, including AI systems, is a product for strict liability purposes. Liability without fault, a 25-year long-stop, and disclosure duties that can reverse the burden of proof.
deadlines.penalty: Civil liability, not administrative fines — but the disclosure duties and the presumption of defectiveness are the expensive part.

deadlines.title: Machinery Regulation 2023/1230 applies in full; Directive 2006/42/EC repealed
deadlines.summary: No grace period and no transition. Machinery must be protected against corruption of the software and control systems that affect safety. Digital instructions permitted. Machines lawfully placed on the market before this date stay under the Directive permanently.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties; the practical cost is a blocked CE marking.

deadlines.title: Cloud switching charges are abolished
deadlines.summary: Providers may no longer charge for switching between cloud providers or for exporting data. Switching charges must be phased down before this date.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties.

deadlines.title: Construction Products Regulation applies
deadlines.summary: The revised CPR replaces the 2011 Regulation, with digital product information and new obligations on manufacturers and importers of construction products.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties; withdrawal from the market.

deadlines.title: Packaging Regulation applies
deadlines.summary: Applies across all 27 Member States with a single rulebook: recyclability requirements, minimum recycled content, and restrictions on single-use packaging. Replaces the Directive.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties; extended producer responsibility costs.

deadlines.title: Battery passport and due diligence obligations
deadlines.summary: Digital battery passport for industrial batteries above 2 kWh, LMT batteries and EV batteries, plus supply chain due diligence obligations.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties; market withdrawal.

deadlines.title: EUDR due diligence in force for large operators
deadlines.summary: Due diligence statements required for cattle, cocoa, coffee, oil palm, rubber, soya and wood placed on or exported from the EU market, with geolocation of plots. Small and micro operators have a longer runway.
deadlines.penalty: Up to 4% of EU turnover, plus exclusion from public procurement.

deadlines.title: Member States must transpose the Pay Transparency Directive
deadlines.summary: Transposition deadline for Directive (EU) 2023/970. Pay transparency in recruitment, a right to information on pay levels, and gender pay gap reporting.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties, including fines and orders to remedy.

deadlines.title: First gender pay gap report for employers with 250+ staff
deadlines.summary: Employers with 250 or more employees report using 2026 pay data. Employers with 150 to 249 employees report on the same date, then every three years.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties.

deadlines.title: Breach notification — 72 hours from awareness
deadlines.summary: Personal data breach notification to the supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware, unless unlikely to result in a risk to rights and freedoms. Notify affected data subjects without undue delay where the risk is high.
deadlines.penalty: Up to €20m or 4% of worldwide annual turnover.

deadlines.title: NIS2 transposition deadline and incident reporting
deadlines.summary: Essential and important entities must report significant incidents: early warning within 24 hours, incident notification within 72 hours, final report within one month.
deadlines.penalty: Up to €10m or 2% of worldwide turnover for essential entities; €7m or 1.4% for important entities.

deadlines.title: Four labour codes come into force
deadlines.summary: Code on Wages, Industrial Relations Code, Code on Social Security and OSH Code replace 29 central labour laws. Section 2(y) of the Code on Wages redefines wages, with a 50% floor on basic plus DA relative to the remuneration base.
deadlines.penalty: Penalties under each Code, plus interest on delayed PF and gratuity.

source.label: Code on Wages 2019, s.2(y); Gazette notification 21 November 2025

deadlines.title: Central Rules notified under all four codes
deadlines.summary: G.S.R. 342(E) and 343(E) and the OSH and Social Security rules supply the forms, registers, returns and timelines that make the Codes operable. Three registers: Form I employee register, Form IV wage register, Form IX attendance register.
deadlines.penalty: Penalties under the Codes for failure to maintain registers.

source.label: Code on Wages (Central) Rules, 2026, G.S.R. 343(E), 8 May 2026

deadlines.title: EPF wage ceiling rises to ₹25,000
deadlines.summary: Statutory wage ceiling for mandatory EPF coverage raised from ₹15,000 to ₹25,000 per month, the first change since September 2014. Maximum employee contribution at the ceiling becomes ₹3,000; EPS share ₹2,082.50.
deadlines.penalty: Damages and interest under section 14B of the EPF Act for short contribution.

source.label: S.O. 5109(E) dated 17 September 2026, under s.2(89) Code on Social Security 2020

deadlines.title: Centre's target date for all states to notify their rules
deadlines.summary: The Labour Secretary stated the Centre was targeting full state-wise coverage by this date. A stated target, not a legal deadline — roughly ten states had notified final rules by late September 2026 and the rest were at draft stage.
deadlines.penalty: None directly; the risk is operating on central rules where the state has notified a different, more employee-favourable rule.

source.label: Ministry of Labour & Employment statement, reported late September 2026

deadlines.title: DPDP Act — breach notification to the Data Protection Board
deadlines.summary: Breach notification to the Data Protection Board and to affected data principals, without delay. Timelines and the 18-month implementation runway are set by the DPDP Rules rather than the Act itself.
deadlines.penalty: Up to ₹250 crore for failure to take reasonable security safeguards; up to ₹200 crore for breach notification failures.

source.label: Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, s.8(6) and s.33; DPDP Rules

deadlines.title: California SB 54 — producers must join a PRO
deadlines.summary: Producers of single-use packaging and plastic food service ware sold in California must join a producer responsibility organisation and pay fees toward recycling targets.
deadlines.penalty: Civil penalties per day for non-participation.

source.label: California SB 54 (2022), Plastic Pollution Prevention and Packaging Producer Responsibility Act

deadlines.title: CSRD as amended by the 2026 Omnibus — phase-in
deadlines.summary: Omnibus I entered into force on 18 March 2026 and removed roughly 80% of companies from mandatory CSRD scope. Listed SMEs are out entirely and the CS3D phased rollout was abolished. Verify whether you are still in scope before building a reporting programme.
deadlines.penalty: Member State penalties for in-scope entities that fail to report.

source.label: Omnibus I (in force 18 March 2026) amending Directive (EU) 2022/2464
